Bytes are asserted to start with %PDF and the extracted text is matched field by field against the snapshot numbers, on Linux with the native pango/cairo stack installed by CI. grep for docx / python-docx / Document( across tests/, modules/, backend/, frontend/ and pyproject.toml returns no hit. There is no DOCX feature in the product, therefore no test and nothing to cover. If DOCX is an announced commercial requirement it is unimplemented, not merely untested.

grep for assinatura / signature / sign_pdf / ICP-Brasil / pyhanko / endesive across tests/, modules/, backend/, frontend/ matches only inspect.signature() reflection calls (modules/local_task_runner.py:28, backend/api.py:527, tests/c14_batch/test_public_api.py:12, tests/acceptance/test_oracles_f01_f16.py:234). No signing, no certificate handling, no signature verification exists.

The manifest hash check, the CSV-injection safety of exported cells and an end-to-end reproduce_from_bundle that must land within tolerance of the original point estimate are all asserted, and the reproduction is repeated from the installed wheel in install-eval-linux.

A torn write is shown not to corrupt the prior snapshot, an abandoned running job becomes interrupted rather than silently succeeded, and the store is shown queryable from a fresh process with no websocket.

The word 'backup' does not appear as a feature anywhere; grep hits under modules/ (job_store.py, project_store.py, evidence_bundle.py) are durable-store and restore-of-state code, covered under recovery above. There is no backup command, no archive/export of the whole data directory, and no restore-from-backup path, therefore no test. Do not read the recovery verdict as backup coverage.

tests: tests/c15_packaging/test_wheel_install_smoke.py::test_clean_venv_install_imports_resources_and_health (run by install-eval-linux with C15_INSTALL_SMOKE=1 since be464a2; still skipped in wide-suite-linux - SKIP-01)
areas.evidence: Packaging is real and verified: wheel/sdist contents, package data, dependency-to-import sync, a clean-venv install that computes a value and emits a PDF, and - since be464a2 - the same job booting /health off the installed wheel (OPT-01, resolved). What is missing is any installer artefact for an end user: there is no .exe/.msi/.pkg/.deb build, only a wheel plus scripts/c15_local/launcher.py. That single gap is why the verdict stays PARTIAL.

grep for updater / auto_update / update_check / atualizacao across tests/, modules/, backend/, scripts/ returns nothing. scripts/c15_local/update_constraints.py is a developer tool that regenerates constraints/linux-py3.txt; it is not a product update channel and must not be counted as coverage. There is no version-check endpoint, no migration-on-upgrade path, and no test of upgrading an installed instance.

No LICENSE file exists at the repo root; pyproject.toml declares no license field and no License:: classifier; there is no third-party licence inventory, no bundled NOTICE, and no product licence-key or entitlement mechanism. grep for licen[cs] across tests/, modules/, backend/ returns no hit. Nothing is covered because nothing exists.

The local-deployment threat model is covered concretely: loopback-only bind, explicit CORS, ws token, per-job payload isolation, path traversal, no pickle deserialization, CSV formula injection, no secrets in defaults, PII stripped from logs. Not covered: authentication/authorization of a multi-user deployment, transport encryption, dependency vulnerability scanning (no pip-audit/safety step in c15-ci.yml), and licence/supply-chain provenance. The product is announced as a local single-user install, which makes the first two arguably out of matrix, but the absence of any dependency-vulnerability gate is a real gap for a commercial release.

findings.title: No requirements matrix exists for MP-COM-20260912/C06
findings.detail: docs/comercial/ did not exist in this repo before this inventory. The eleven areas inventoried here come from the C06 task statement. Nothing in the repo declares which of them are obligatory for the commercial release, so 'applicable requirement' cannot be verified against a source document. Any coverage claim in this inventory is coverage against an unratified list.

findings.title: Digital signature, DOCX, licences and product update are entirely absent from the product
findings.detail: Four of the eleven areas have no implementation at all, hence no test: digital signature (only inspect.signature reflection hits), DOCX generation (zero hits repo-wide), licences (no LICENSE file, no license field in pyproject.toml, no third-party inventory, no entitlement mechanism) and update (no updater; scripts/c15_local/update_constraints.py is a dev tool, not a product update channel). These are ABSENT, not PARTIAL.

findings.title: C15_INSTALL_SMOKE was set by no CI job, so the installed-artifact /health property was asserted nowhere
findings.detail: tests/c15_packaging/test_wheel_install_smoke.py is skipif-gated on C15_INSTALL_SMOKE, which grep finds in no file under .github/. Its docstring claims 'CI runs it in the dedicated install-smoke job'; that job does not exist. INTEGRATION.md:122 says it is covered by install-eval-linux, but install-eval-linux never boots a server and never calls /health. The closest health test, tests/c15_packaging/test_launcher_command.py::test_backend_process_health_on_loopback, runs against the editable checkout, not the installed wheel. Class (b). Hardened by exhaustive check: grep -rn 'wait_for_health|/health' over tests/, scripts/ and backend/ shows every other health boot runs against the editable checkout - test_launcher_command.py:95, c17_integration/test_r17_hardening.py:218, acceptance/test_e2e_ui.py:117, p04/test_browser_composed.py:105 - or via fastapi TestClient in-process (tests/test_api.py:15, acceptance/test_e2e_http.py:23). No test other than the skipped one boots a server from a non-editable installed distribution. RESOLUTION: be464a2 added a step to install-eval-linux with env C15_INSTALL_SMOKE: "1" that runs pytest tests/c15_packaging/test_wheel_install_smoke.py; the test boots uvicorn with the clean venv's interpreter and asserts /health returns status=healthy (test_wheel_install_smoke.py:113-128). A regression guard, tests/c15_packaging/test_workflow_triggers.py::test_install_smoke_flag_is_actually_set_by_a_job, fails if the setter is ever removed. INTEGRATION.md:122's 'coberto por install-eval-linux' is now true, by a mechanism that did not exist when that line was written. Retained, not deleted: the negative was real.

findings.title: The aggregator's evidence verification, including the strict P04 extensions run, did not execute in CI (original R20-A defect; independently rediscovered, already fixed)
findings.detail: This is an accurate description of the original R20-A defect and was reached independently here. It was however ALREADY FIXED when this document first measured: 65cb121 landed at 2026-09-12T01:58:30Z and revision 1 measured at 02:01:23Z, having re-collected tests against the new HEAD without re-reading the workflow, so it described the parent 8d66c79 and stamped it 65cb121. WHAT THE DEFECT WAS: verify_artifacts() runs only when --artifacts-dir is passed, and the acceptance job passed only --required-jobs and --results-json, so the strict-extensions check (aggregate_required.py:154-156), the mode check (:130-132), the SHA check (:170-173) and the wide-test floor never ran; combined with p04-harness running --mode diagnose-base, no CI path could turn a missing P01/P02/P03 extension on the composed candidate into a red build. STATE AT be464a2: the acceptance job passes --artifacts-dir evidence --expected-sha "$CANDIDATE_SHA" --min-wide-tests 700 --p04-mode accept-candidate, and p04-harness runs --mode accept-candidate, which exports P04_REQUIRE_EXTENSIONS=1 (run.py:124-125) and records an 'extensions' run in run.json (run.py:172-191). A missing extension does now make the build red. Guarded by tests/c15_packaging/test_workflow_triggers.py::test_aggregator_opens_the_evidence_not_only_the_job_results and ::test_p04_harness_job_accepts_the_candidate_strictly. CORRECTION: revision 1 cited aggregate_required.py:135-136 for the strict-extensions check and main() at :243; :135-136 is the exit_code check and main() is at :241. The strict-extensions check is at :154-156.

findings.title: The collected test total is not reproducible, and quoting the SHA does not fix that
findings.detail: Collections at 705, 733, 739, 756 and 852 were observed on this worktree while sibling C06 agents wrote test files into it. 852 was confirmed at be464a2 by two consecutive collections whose node-id lists are byte-identical. THE INSTABILITY DISCLOSURE STANDS. The remedy proposed in revision 1 - 'any downstream document quoting a bare total must quote the SHA with it' - DOES NOT WORK, because 39 of the 852 come from two UNTRACKED files (tests/pro_workflow/p04/test_mutations_commercial.py 21, tests/pro_workflow/p04/test_metamorphic_reference.py 18) that no commit determines; an independent verifier's re-run over a superset tree reported 832, at a tree whose SHA would have been quoted as authority for a different number (that 832 is the verifier's measurement, not one taken here). WORKING REMEDY: quote the tracked-file total (813 at be464a2) and label it as such - see collected_total.how_to_quote for why even 813 is only approachable, not exactly recomputable, from a clean checkout; or quote 852 together with `git status --porcelain tests/` showing exactly which untracked test files were present; or do not use a collected total as a headline number at all.

findings.title: No dependency-vulnerability or supply-chain gate for a commercial release
findings.detail: .github/workflows/c15-ci.yml has no pip-audit, safety, SBOM or licence-scan step. constraints/linux-py3.txt pins versions and tests/c15_packaging/test_dependency_sync.py verifies the pins match the imports, but nothing checks those pins against a vulnerability database or records the licences of the pinned dependencies. Combined with FIND-02's absent licence file, the supply-chain posture of the release is unverified. CROSS-REFERENCE: the sibling C06 deliverable docs/comercial/c06/security_supply_chain.md reaches the same conclusion independently and records it as BLOCKED items B1 and B2 - pip-audit and safety are absent from every inspected interpreter and from PATH, and no SBOM generator is installed, so no vulnerability scan and no transitive licence review were performed. That document also records a concrete licence obligation (xlrd 2.0.2 is BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-4-Clause; the BSD-4-Clause portion requires an attribution acknowledgment in redistributions), which reinforces the licences=ABSENT verdict here: the repo ships no LICENSE and no third-party notices file to carry that acknowledgment. Consolidation should treat FIND-07 and that document's B1/B2/F2 as one finding.

findings.title: c15-tests-windows cannot block the gate
findings.detail: The Windows job was absent from the acceptance job's --required-jobs list, so a Windows failure was not a red build. RESOLUTION: at be464a2 c15-tests-windows is in --required-jobs and in the acceptance job's needs, pinned by tests/c15_packaging/test_workflow_triggers.py::test_windows_blocks_the_gate. This makes the Windows packaging tests blocking; it is still not a Windows readiness claim, since launcher --check-pdf remains continue-on-error and docs/campaigns/MP-PRO-20260911/OVERVIEW.md:4 does not announce Windows PDF.

findings.title: Lint covers only C15/P04-owned paths
findings.detail: The lint job's flake8 invocation enumerates a fixed file list; modules/, backend/ and frontend/ at large are not linted. Not a correctness defect, but the gate does not mean 'the codebase lints'.

not_claimed: The suite was not executed; only collection was run. No pass/fail claim is made.
